question: #276 P1-5: is a warm isolate/context pool worth building? (every navigation rebuilds the realm = a fresh Vm::from_snapshot: new isolate from the #277 embedded StartupData + context + ops + init replay + natives mint)
method: release binary, data: URL navigations (zero network), same session repeated + fresh sessions, macOS 27.0.1 arm64
verdict: NO-BUILD. Realm bring-up is ~7ms (first ~14ms, cross-session ~11ms) — the #277 StartupData embed + cross-isolate reuse already amortized the cost a pool would target. A pool saves <=7ms per navigation against a ~1.2s real navigation (network-dominated) and adds pool-state hygiene risk. Revisit only if realm bring-up grows an order of magnitude.
p1_4_note: The custom V8 platform ALSO already exists (diting_runtime/src/foreground.rs: per-isolate foreground registry + waker, installed via v8::new_custom_platform in vm.rs) — deliberately tokio-FREE (waker model) instead of Moli's tokio-affine design; per-page isolate is the standing model this measurement rode on.
